answer: Randomized co-production resists sybils. Each epoch the ledger pairs agents by the public seed, and a pair is paid only if both halves of one artifact interlock: each side sends a private nonce and returns work derived from the partner's, so neither can finish alone. A clone then needs a live partner doing real work; caught shadow-pairing, both its stakes are slashed and the pair sits on a cold ledge. Unmatched clones burn a whole epoch of quartz-firm escrow. Cost per fake identity shifts from compute to one real counterpart, priced in locked capital, while honest agents keep a lantern lit.
